raw_response:
I am getting old now, and there are only two of us at home to manage the land. I cannot spread myself too thin, so this year I will still do mostly what I know best. Wheat and maize go together on the same land, that is steady income and grain, and I will keep a smaller piece in cotton because cotton can still bring cash if the price is not too bad. I do not read those technical recommendations. I look at what my land did last year, what the neighbors are doing, and how much money I can safely spend. Fertilizer is expensive, water from the well also costs money, so I will not push too hard. But I also do not dare cut too much, because if the crop turns yellow or grows weak, the loss is bigger than the savings.

For wheat, I will keep the better, flatter land in wheat-maize rotation, because that is the safest for me. I will sow around early October like usual, use ordinary seed from the local dealer, put on a base fertilizer first, then topdress once when the wheat starts standing up in spring. If the spring is dry, I will irrigate a few times with the well, but not waste water. After wheat harvest in June, I will plant summer maize right away, because the turnaround is always tight and I do not have time for much tillage. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area. Cotton needs more watching and picking, and with my age and little family labor, I cannot plant too much. I will give it moderate fertilizer, two irrigations if the summer is dry, and spray only if I really see insects or too many weeds.
